properties.decision: UNSETTLED. The instance is fixed; the class is not. Two dev_storyflow seats independently measured that the `brainstorm` skill instructed them to call `set_decision_status(proposed)` because "add_decision defaults to accepted" — behaviour that changed on 2026-07-25 and is dated in add_decision's own description — so a conscientious agent made a redundant write on every brainstormed idea. PR #102 corrected the text on 2026-08-08. WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS THE SHAPE OF THE GUARD, and three were offered: (a) let a skill ASSERT the defaults it relies on, so skill_lint fails loudly at the moment the default changes rather than the text aging quietly; (b) GENERATE the sentence from the tool's actual default at build time, so it cannot disagree; (c) forbid a skill from naming a default at all and require it to state the RELATION instead — "confirm the returned status is `proposed`" — which stays true across any default change and needs no new machinery. THERE IS AN OBVIOUS HOME: skill_lint.py already enforces that every tool a skill NAMES is served, and is run in CI on every push; asserting a default is the same kind of contract one field deeper.
properties.name: OPEN — when a served skill's text depends on a served tool's DEFAULT, should that dependency be asserted so the build breaks when the default moves?
properties.rationale: Worth a decision rather than a fix note because of what the reporters said about it, which generalises past this skill: a served skill and a served tool ship from the SAME BINARY and disagreed about that binary's behaviour — the one place this class of drift should be impossible. And the skill is the half a session reads BEFORE acting, so it is the half that silently teaches the wrong model; here it taught it with emphasis ("This call is not optional"), which is exactly the wording that survives a skim. Their formulation is the reusable one: A RULE PINNED TO A BEHAVIOUR MUST NAME HOW TO RE-CHECK IT, NEVER JUST ITS VERDICT. Reported 2026-08-08 by dragon Boss f96eccd3 and api-boss 5d608b85, both by RUNNING it and reading the echo; api-boss stated their own bound honestly, that they did not test whether the redundant call is harmful, only that it is unnecessary.
